Subject: Re: Fwd: Unexpected quality drop in Summarize+Answer A/B — routing options and quick mitigations

On our side: we can implement tenant-level routing flips within ~15 minutes once we sign the routing change; it’s a config push (no deploy). Options:

A) Route Acme back to B cohort only (fastest) — minimal risk, immediate mitigation
B) Route Acme to a quantized fallback variant of A (lower-latency config) — preserves A behavior but may degrade quality in other ways
C) Apply prefix-level prompt guard (server-side) that adds a verification step for extraction; this buys time but increases latency ~120–200ms per request.

I attached diff_report.csv that highlights request-level deltas between cohorts (latency, token counts, error flags). Early read: A is producing more longer-form filler for specific invoice-type examples — looks like a prompt phrasing change that broadens generation.

Operationally I recommend Option A now (route back to B), then we do a controlled test with Option C on a small sample to see if we can preserve A’s improvements while avoiding the hallucinations. If tests fail, we either keep B or iterate prompt.

ETA: I can flip routing now if Ben confirms with the customer. I’ll also prepare a short rollback playbook (attached).

Karthik
Principal Product Engineer, Redwood Inference
